Hi Tom / Morgan —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on integration scope and the items your engineering team asked to see:

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary integration: server-side calls from Nimbus backend to Redwood for chat + structured tool-calling (order review & billing lookups).
- Embeddings/reranker will be used for document search (patient protocols) with nightly re-indexing.
- Auth: prefer short-lived mTLS tokens for Dedicated pockets, fallback to API key with request-scoped service tokens for Hosted.
- Non-functional requirements: 50 reqs/sec peak for chat, average 400 tokens/response, P95 latency target < 300ms.
- Concern: rate limiting behavior under bursty traffic and safe retry/idempotency semantics for duplicate webhook retries.

Requested deliverables (we'll deliver by EOD Thu):
1) Simple SDK startup guide tailored to your Go + Node services (auth snippet, retry middleware sample).
2) Routing recommendations: how to steer dev/test to hosted while production hits your Dedicated pool.
3) Quota & throttling playbook: expected rate limits, quota topologies, retry/backoff guidelines including idempotency-key conventions.
4) Embeddings pipeline notes: batch size, warm-up, and small reranker template.

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa: technical write-up + code samples (SDK snippets, idempotency header examples).
- Sergio: pricing/quota proposal and draft MSA language for limits and burst policy.
- Soojin: schedule a 30-min engineering sync for Friday if that works for your team.

Attachments: nimbus-technical-questions.pdf (your list), soojin-call-notes-20260412.txt (internal notes).

If that matches your expectations, I’ll queue the artifacts. Confirm Friday 11am PT for the engineering sync?

Cheers,

1) For idempotency: our backend will generate a stable request ID for user-driven actions (UI-initiated). For async webhooks from our partners we need guidance on how Redwood expects to receive idempotency keys — will your platform pass back the same header on retried responses?

2) For embeddings: how granular should our vectors be for patient protocols? We have ~60K documents and expect daily diffs of ~500 documents.

3) Quota: if we buy a Dedicated pool, can we set hard caps per-route (e.g., embeddings vs. chat) and reserve burst capacity for latency-critical paths? Also need to understand SLA behavior when a route hits quota.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Tom —

Thanks for the follow-ups. I put together a technical note + small code samples below (summarized). Full snippets and a runnable gist are in the link I dropped in related_links.

Short answers first:
- Idempotency: Redwood respects the Idempotency-Key header on mutating endpoints. If you include a stable idempotency key (prefer client-generated UUIDv4 per user action) we guarantee at-most-once semantics across retries for the same key within the retention window (configurable; default 24h for Hosted, customer-configurable for Dedicated).
- Retry echo: we will echo back the Idempotency-Key in the response headers and include an X-Redwood-Retry-Count header when requests are retried internally.
- Quotas & routing: Dedicated supports per-route reservations. You can allocate N GPUs to chat and M to embeddings and configure reserve/burst buckets. When a route hits quota the routing policy can: 1) queue (wait), 2) fallback to lower-cost quantized model, or 3) spill to Hosted fallback (if allowed).

Sample retry/backoff middleware (pseudo-JS):
- Use exponential backoff with jitter: base=200ms, factor=2, max=10s, attempts=5.
- On 429/503 return: retry if Idempotency-Key present and request is idempotent or marked safe to retry (we suggest idempotency for all mutating calls).
- Include X-Request-Id (server-generated) on every request and return it in responses so you can trace duplicates.

Example headers we recommend:
- Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>
- Idempotency-Key: <client-uuid>
- X-Request-Id: <generated-by-client-or-proxy>

Embeddings guidance:
- For 60K docs with 500 daily diffs: batch index in 2k doc batches during off-peak windows; use per-batch retry with idempotency keyed by batch-id.
- Use cosine similarity + top-k rerank (k=10) by default; we can provide a small reranker model tuned for medical language if needed.

Attachments referenced: I attached a one-pager with retention windows and quota semantics (nimbus-technical-questions.pdf).

I’ll bring a short runbook to the Friday call: code deploy checklist, test prompts for latency SLAs, and a fallback flow example.

--
